items.item_text: Data Collection/Communication: 1.Performs respiratory assessment based on gestational age, maternal factors and documented on the Newborn Stabilization/Resuscitation Record. 2.Remains current with on going data collection by documenting treatments, ABGs, changes in Respiratory status and observations. 3. Provides a complete patient report when handing over care to on coming staff.

Respiratory Evaluation: 4. Evaluates the effectiveness of respiratory care by: a.Demonstrates ability to carry out medical orders and collaborates with the RN to consider er appropriateness of orders in relationship to current therapy and infant condition. b. Observes and documents infants response to therapeutic interventions. c. Collaborates with RN to interpret clinical assessment and provide appropriate intervention. Notifies physician of significant airway/respiratory changes in infant. d. Reviews chest films at least once per shift and identifies significant changes and infant condition.

Technical Skills: 5. Demonstrates competency in selected psychomotor skills and performs technical procedures as evidenced by: a. Remaining competent in neonatal intubation, use of conventional and oscillator vents, obtaining specimens, and newborn resuscitation. b. Ability to assist physicians both in NICU and NICU surgical area. c. Ability to trouble shoot equipment, remain current with new and established supplies/equipment. d. Successfully perform selected phlebotomy procedures.

Emergency Response: 6. Demonstrates ability to perform effectively in emergency situations in NICU/SCN or Family Birth Center. a. Collaboratively performs NRP duties with RN. b. Responds to Code Blue situations within NICU or Family Birth Center. c. Anticipate and assist with peer/unit needs during emergency/code situations without requiring direction.
Responds to Emergency Department requests for attendance at imminent deliveries, with resuscitation bed, scale, and emergency drugs.
Completes inventory of emergency and resuscitation equipment at the beginning of each shift in delivery area, including operating suites, and replaces any missing supplies, equipment, etc.
Basic Life Support from the American Heart Association.
